summary: L. P. N. Perera was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a supervisor at the Vidyodaya Campus of the University of Sri Lanka and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and the University of Paris. Working in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies, he served as Professor of Central Asian Languages at Eötvös Loránd University (1940–1974).

Lajos Lóczy (1849–1920) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Zurich and ETH Zurich. He held a post at the Hungarian National Museum (1874) and was Professor of Geography at Eötvös Loránd University (1889).
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshman Sarup (1894–1946) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as University Professor of Sanskrit at Panjab University, where he is attested in 1947.
Lakshmanacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He held a teaching post at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura, attested in 1889 and 1900.
Lakshmi Swaminathan (1914–2012) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Queen Mary's College and Madras Medical College. She later served as a lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under G. C. Pande. Active in Buddhist and religious studies and Indology, he held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Harvard, Haverford, Amherst, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar who served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested in 1939.
Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist who served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and, attested in 2026, as Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford.

Lama Jampa Thaye (b. 1952), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earned a PhD from the University of Manchester and trained under several traditional Tibetan teachers. He serves on the international teaching faculty at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche (b. 1935) studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under multiple traditional teachers, including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Isebaert (b. 1955) is a linguist, Indologist, and Central Asian scholar who studied under Albert Joris van Windekens. He served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain, attested in 2013.

Lambert Schmithausen (b. 1939) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He was an associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and served at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lan Wu is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. from Columbia University (2008–2016). She served as Assistant Professor at the University of New Mexico (2015–2016) and Associate Professor at Mount Holyoke College (2023).

Lance E. Nelson, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986. He served as a professor at the University of San Diego, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2021.

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Cambridge under H. W. Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–1996) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and served as President of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).
Lancelot Wilkinson (1805–1841) was an Indologist who studied at the East India Company College (~1822–1823) and joined the Bombay Civil Service in 1822.
